title: Penang vs Ipoh: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Penang for first-timers, hawker variety, and UNESCO heritage. Ipoh for dim sum, cave temples, and a slower pace. Daily budget: Penang MYR 100–180 vs Ipoh MYR 70–130.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: Penang has world-class hawker density and variety. Ipoh wins on dim sum and kai si hor fun.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Ipoh runs 20–30% cheaper than Penang across accommodation, food, and transport.

categories.name: Heritage & Culture
categories.summary: George Town is a UNESCO World Heritage city with dense, walkable heritage. Ipoh has colonial charm and growing street art.

categories.name: Temples & Nature
categories.summary: Penang has Kek Lok Si and Penang Hill. Ipoh has Sam Poh Tong cave temples and Kellie's Castle.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Penang has Batu Ferringhi. Ipoh has no beach access.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: George Town is walkable with free bus. Ipoh needs Grab or scooter for most attractions.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Penang connects to Langkawi, Cameron Highlands, and KL. Ipoh is the best base for Cameron Highlands.

categories.name: Dim Sum
categories.summary: Ipoh's dim sum is among the best in Malaysia — Penangites drive 2 hours specifically for it.

faq.question: Is Penang or Ipoh better for first-time visitors to Malaysia?
faq.answer: Penang is the stronger first-time pick with more variety, UNESCO heritage, and beach access.

faq.question: How far is Penang from Ipoh?
faq.answer: About 165 km, 2–2.5 hours by bus (MYR 15–25) or KTM ETS train (MYR 18–35).

faq.question: Which city has better food?
faq.answer: Penang wins on variety. Ipoh wins on dim sum and kai si hor fun. Serious foodies should do both.
